annotations.text:
Shipping D · axis: tier chooser.
Why: the two tiers become two equal white cards with the price as a 44px Newsreader numeral and a what-is-included list, so a buyer comparing $185 against $350 reads the difference as five checked lines per card instead of two paragraphs; every line is a fact already in the round-1 tier copy or intro, and one clay CTA sits under both cards. Measured: Desktop 1,087px, Tablet 1,140px, Mobile 1,753px.
Trade-off: it is the tallest of the three at every width, and the tallest on the page at 390 by 357px over F, because the two lists stack; it also drops the crate photo entirely.

(Recommended) Shipping E · axis: route.
Why: the route line puts both prices on the trip itself, Midland, TX to your airport ($185) to your door ($350), in the order the bird travels, and it keeps the crate photo beside the route. Measured it is the shortest of the three at Desktop, 981px against F 1,021 and D 1,087, and at Mobile, 1,380px against F 1,396 and D 1,753, where the line turns vertical with three 20px nodes down the left.
Trade-off: it is the tallest at Tablet, 1,190px against F 1,028 and D 1,140, because the photo stacks above the route there; and at Desktop the three stop descriptions sit in 219px centered columns at 13px, the narrowest measure on the page.

Shipping F · axis: fact grid.
Why: six labelled definitions (tier, price, carrier and route, timing, crate, arrival) answer the six shipping questions without card chrome, beside the crate photo at 22px radius, which is the layout closest to the live section (photo beside copy) and so the cheapest to adopt. Measured it is the shortest at Tablet, 1,028px against D 1,140 and E 1,190, and within 40px of the shortest at Desktop (1,021) and 16px at Mobile (1,396).
Trade-off: the two prices share one 15px value cell instead of leading their tiers, so a reader scanning for a figure finds it third, after Tier, and the grid carries no tier descriptions at all.
